chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'We wear Ihram from the road of Al-Basra, and we do not know the boundary of the width of Al-Aqeeq.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Wear Ihram from Wajra.'

key_terms.أَحْرِمْ: Wear Ihram (enter the state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.عَرْضِ الْعَقِيقِ: The width of Al-Aqeeq (a geographical region)

ai.seo_question: Where should one wear Ihram if the boundary of Al-Aqeeq is unknown?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) provides a precise geographical marker, Wajrah, for entering the state of Ihram when the exact boundary of the natural valley (Aqiq) is unknown, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical adaptability in ritual law. This hadith illustrates the principle of using recognizable landmarks to determine the Miqat, ensuring the validity of the pilgrimage even in the absence of fixed, universally known coordinates.
